title: Capital Market Vs Money Market
definition: The financial system is bifurcated into the money market, which handles short-term funding and liquidity needs (up to one year), and the capital market, which channels medium to long-term funds for permanent capital formation and investments exceeding one year.
importanceInUpsc: Frequently tested in UPSC Prelims regarding instruments, regulators (RBI vs SEBI), and liquidity management, as well as in Mains (GS-3 Mobilization of Resources, Growth, and Development).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Capital Market Vs Money Market.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Role of Reserve Bank of India
